title_en: China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Dalian Office v. Liaoning Huaxi Group Corporation et al. — loan guarantee dispute (appeal)
keywords_en: civil; dispute over loan guarantee; second instance; Supreme People's Court; Liaoning Province; legal person; financial institution; Contract Law; Guarantee Law; determination of ambiguous guarantee period; effect of re-confirmation after expiry of limitation of action for principal debt on guarantee liability; partially sustained; loan contract; guarantee; assignment of creditor's rights; collection notice; suretyship; dispute over loan guarantee involving Xi Group Company, et al.
full_text_en:
China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Dalian Branch v.  
Liaoning Huaxi Group Corporation, et al. — dispute over loan and guarantee  

Supreme People's Court  
Civil Judgment  

(2003) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 93  

Appellant: China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Dalian Branch.  
Address: No. 9 Yan'an Road, Zhongshan District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province.  
Responsible Person: Zhu Shanyun, General Manager of the Branch.  
Agent ad litem: Li Long, lawyer of Liaoning Hengxin Law Firm.  

Respondent: Liaoning Huaxi Group Corporation.  
Address: No. 95 Renmin Road, Zhongshan District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province.  
Legal Representative: Wei Wei, Chairman of the Board.  
Agent ad litem: Zheng Shengnan, employee of the Corporation.  

Respondent: Liaoning Times Group Co., Ltd.  
Address: No. 7 Gangwan Street, Zhongshan District, Dalian City, Liaoning Province.  
Legal Representative: Fan Xiaoyuan, Chairman of the Board.  
Agent ad litem: Sun Yantao, lawyer of Liaoning Huaxuan Law Firm.  

Respondent: Liaoning Animal Products Import and Export Company.  
Address: No. 95 Renmin Road, Zhongshan District, Dalian City.  
Legal Representative: Wang Yupeng, General Manager of the Company.  
Agent ad litem: Fu Yuling, employee of the Company.  

The appellant, China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Dalian Branch, appealed against the civil judgment (2002) Liao Min San Chu Zi No. 70 rendered by the Liaoning High People's Court in the case of a dispute over loan and guarantee with the respondents Liaoning Huaxi Group Corporation, Liaoning Times Group Co., Ltd., and Liaoning Animal Products Import and Export Company. This Court filed the appeal. The Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Presiding Judge Jiang Bixin, Judges Song Xiaoming and Cao Shibing as members. The case was publicly heard on August 26, 2003, with court clerk Xia Dongxia keeping the record. The case is now concluded.  

The court of first instance found the following facts:  
On January 14, 1995, Liaoning Animal Products Import and Export Company (hereinafter referred to as Animal Products Company) entered into a foreign exchange loan contract numbered Hui Liu Zi No. 95001 with Liaoning Branch of Bank of China (hereinafter referred to as Provincial BOC). The contract stipulated: the loan amount was USD 2,000,000 for foreign exchange working capital; the loan purpose was to import mink and fox skins for processing and exporting garments; the loan interest rate was to be the foreign exchange working capital loan rate published by Bank of China, with a 10% increase; the loan term was six months. On January 4 of the same year, Liaoning Garment Import and Export Company (the predecessor of Liaoning Times Group Co., Ltd., hereinafter referred to as Times Company), acting as the guarantor, issued an irrevocable letter of guarantee to Provincial BOC. The letter of guarantee promised: this guarantee is an unconditional irrevocable guarantee, with a guaranteed amount of USD 2,000,000 or the equivalent in Renminbi of USD 2,000,000, plus the loan interest and expenses incurred under the loan; this guarantee is to guarantee the repayment of all or part of the overdue principal and interest of the borrower under the loan contract numbered Hui Liu Zi No. 95001, and agrees to repay the borrower's overdue principal and interest within 14 days after receiving written notice from Provincial BOC; this guarantee is a continuous guarantee and indemnity, unaffected by any instructions received by the borrower from higher authorities or any agreements or documents signed between the borrower and any unit; this guarantee shall take effect from the date of signing and shall automatically expire when all principal, interest and expenses owed by the borrower are fully repaid. After the contract was signed, Provincial BOC disbursed USD 830,577.69 and USD 1,169,422.31 to Animal Products Company on January 16 and January 23, 1995, respectively, totaling USD 2,000,000. On January 23, 1995, Animal Products Company used USD 1,169,422.31 and USD 340,692.60 to repay USD 1,500,000 under the loan contract numbered 94010 in two installments. On October 28, 1997, Animal Products Company and Provincial BOC entered into a loan contract numbered Liao Zhong Yin Dai Zi 97000538. The contract stipulated: the loan type was a professional foreign trade enterprise loan; the loan amount was RMB 25,200,000; the loan purpose was to purchase export commodities; the interest rate was 9.504% per annum; the loan term was from October 28, 1997 to September 28, 1998. After the contract was signed, Provincial BOC fulfilled its contractual obligations and transferred RMB 25,200,000 to Animal Products Company's account on October 28, 1997. Upon maturity, Animal Products Company failed to repay the debt on time. Provincial BOC sent loan collection notices to Animal Products Company on August 31, 1999 and September 13, 1999, respectively, and Animal Products Company affixed its seal to confirm receipt on each notice. On May 31, 2000, Provincial BOC and China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Dalian Branch (hereinafter referred to as Orient Company) entered into a creditor's rights transfer agreement, agreeing to transfer to Orient Company the creditor's rights of Provincial BOC against Animal Products Company for the loan principal of RMB 223,750,000 and USD 3,996,901.50, plus accrued interest. On the same day, Provincial BOC issued a notice of transfer of creditor's rights to Animal Products Company. Animal Products Company, after receiving the notice of transfer, affixed its seal to confirm. On September 29, 2001, Orient Company published an announcement in Liaoning Daily to issue a collection notice to all debtors and guarantors whose creditor's rights were transferred.

The court of first instance also found: On September 8, 1993, Animal Products Company, as the organizing unit, applied to the Liaoning Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce to establish Liaoning Huaxi Group Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Huaxi Group). The company's articles of association clearly stated that Huaxi Group was an export-oriented, public-owned comprehensive commercial and trade enterprise restructured from the original Liaoning Animal Products Import and Export Company, and that Animal Products Company was the core enterprise of Huaxi Group.

On August 8, 2002, Orient Company filed a lawsuit with the Liaoning High People's Court, requesting a judgment ordering the debtor, Animal Products Company, to bear the legal liability for repaying the loan principal and interest; ordering Times Company to bear the guarantee liability for the loan principal and interest under the loan contract numbered 95001; and on the ground that Animal Products Company had invested all its assets into Huaxi Group, rendering Animal Products Company virtually defunct, requesting a judgment ordering Huaxi Group to bear legal liability for Animal Products Company's debts.

The court of first instance held: The loan contracts between Animal Products Company and Provincial BOC, the irrevocable letter of guarantee issued by Times Company, and the creditor's rights transfer agreement between Provincial BOC and Orient Company were all the true expressions of the parties' intentions, did not violate mandatory provisions of laws and regulations, and were legal and valid. Animal Products Company should repay the debt owing to Orient Company in accordance with the two loan contracts. The loan contract numbered 95001 was signed before the Security Law came into effect, with a performance period of six months. The guarantee letter of Times Company stipulated the guarantee period as "effective from the date of signing and automatically expires when all principal, interest and expenses owed by the borrower are fully repaid." According to the relevant judicial interpretations of the Supreme People's Court, this should be deemed as an unclear agreement on the guarantee period. Where the guarantee period is unclear, the guarantor shall bear liability within the period during which the guaranteed party bears liability. That guarantee period is two years within the statute of limitations, and its nature should be considered a preclusive period. Regardless of whether the statute of limitations is interrupted or suspended, as long as the creditor fails to assert its rights against the guarantor within two years after the expiration of the main contract performance period, the guarantor may be exonerated. In this case, the performance period of the contract numbered 95001 was six months, i.e., due on July 14, 1995. The creditor, Provincial BOC, should have asserted its rights against the guarantor, Times Company, before July 14, 1997. However, the creditor, Orient Company, only asserted its rights against the guarantor through publication of an announcement in Liaoning Daily on September 29, 2001, which was far beyond the guarantee period. According to regulations, the guarantor, Times Company, should be exonerated. The loan contract numbered 95001 matured on July 14, 1995. The debtor, Animal Products Company, repaid five installments of loan interest to Provincial BOC from June 15, 1995 to July 31, 1996. Therefore, the statute of limitations for the principal debt should start from August 1, 1996 and expire on July 31, 1998. Provincial BOC sent loan collection notices to Animal Products Company on August 31, 1999 and September 13, 1999, which was beyond the statute of limitations period. Animal Products Company affixed its seal to confirm on the collection notices. According to the provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Reply (Fa Shi (1999) No. 7), this should be deemed as a reaffirmation of the original debt by Animal Products Company. The Supreme People's Court's Notice (2002) No. 144 provides that if a guarantee contract signed before the Security Law came into effect did not specify a guarantee period or specified it unclearly, and the principal debt has not exceeded the statute of limitations, and the creditor has not asserted its rights against the guarantor, the creditor may assert its rights against the guarantor within six months from the date of issuance of this notice. In this case, the principal debt had already exceeded the statute of limitations. After the statute of limitations had expired, the debtor, Animal Products Company, reaffirmed the creditor's rights. This was a disposition by the debtor, Animal Products Company, of its own rights and had no relation to the guarantor, Times Company. After the statute of limitations for the principal debt had expired, the creditor and debtor reaffirmed the original debt. Since the original principal debt had once exceeded the statute of limitations, according to the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Document Fa Fa (1994) No. 8, unless the guarantor clearly provides a guarantee for the reaffirmed principal debt, the guarantor shall no longer bear the guarantee liability. Since Times Company did not clearly express that it would provide a guarantee for the reaffirmed principal debt between Orient Company and Animal Products Company, the guarantor, Times Company, no longer bears guarantee liability. Times Company's defense is reasonable and should be supported. Although Huaxi Group was established upon the application of Animal Products Company, both Huaxi Group and Animal Products Company exist as independent enterprise legal persons. Animal Products Company entered into loan contracts with Provincial BOC and formed creditor-debtor relationships after Huaxi Group was established. Animal Products Company's debts were caused by its own independent corporate acts and have no relation to Huaxi Group. Therefore, Animal Products Company should bear responsibility for repaying its debts. Although Huaxi Group submitted "Application for Extension of USD Loan" to the Foreign Exchange Credit Department of Provincial BOC in its own name on July 7, 1995, this application was not agreed to by Provincial BOC, and this application alone cannot establish that Huaxi Group replaced Animal Products Company as the borrower. Animal Products Company was both the signatory and the performing party to the contract. Provincial BOC and Orient Company have consistently asserted their rights against Animal Products Company, not against Huaxi Group. According to the industrial and commercial registration, Huaxi Group and Animal Products Company are independent enterprise legal persons, and there is no evidence that Huaxi Group assumed the creditor's rights and debts of Animal Products Company. Animal Products Company still exists as an independent enterprise legal person. Therefore, Huaxi Group should not be liable for Animal Products Company's debts. In conclusion, in accordance with Article 90 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 29 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Guarantee in the Trial of Economic Contract Disputes, the court made the following judgment: 1. The defendant, Liaoning Animal Products Import and Export Company, shall, within 15 days after this judgment takes effect, repay the plaintiff, China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Dalian Branch, the debt of USD 2,000,000 and interest of USD 623,386.17 as of May 31, 2000 (default interest from June 1, 2000 until the date of full payment shall be calculated at the overdue payment default interest rate set by the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period); 2. The defendant, Liaoning Animal Products Import and Export Company, shall, within 15 days after this judgment takes effect, repay the plaintiff, China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Dalian Branch, the debt of RMB 25,200,000 and interest of RMB 14,559,358.88 as of May 31, 2000 (default interest from June 1, 2000 until the date of full payment shall be calculated at the overdue payment default interest rate set by the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period); 3. The claim of the plaintiff, China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Dalian Branch, that the defendant, Liaoning Times Group Co., Ltd., bear joint and several liability for the debt of USD 2,000,000 and interest owed by the defendant, Liaoning Animal Products Import and Export Company, is dismissed; 4. The claim of the plaintiff, China Orient Asset Management Corporation, Dalian Branch, against the defendant, Liaoning Huaxi Group Corporation, is dismissed. The case acceptance fee and preservation fee are reduced by half: the case acceptance fee is RMB 158,640, the preservation fee is RMB 152,760, totaling RMB 311,400, to be borne by the defendant, Liaoning Animal Products Import and Export Company.

Orient Company, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Liaoning High People's Court, appealed to this Court, arguing: 1. Huaxi Group should bear liability. The debtor, Animal Products Company, invested all its assets to establish Huaxi Group in 1995. As the core enterprise of Huaxi Group, Animal Products Company effectively had no independent assets for operation; all its assets were merged into Huaxi Group, losing the ability to independently bear civil liability. In January 1995, Animal Products Company signed the loan contract numbered 95001 with Provincial BOC. On July 7, 1995, Huaxi Group applied to Provincial BOC for an extension of this loan in its own name, indicating that Huaxi Group acknowledged its actual borrower status. 2. Times Company should bear guarantee liability. Times Company promised in its guarantee letter that "this guarantee shall remain valid when the Liaoning Branch of Bank of China agrees to the borrower Animal Products Company's extension of repayment." In this case, Provincial BOC agreed to Animal Products Company's extension, requiring repayment by September 1999. The appellant also issued a "Notice of Transfer of Creditor's Rights" to the borrower in May 2000, demanding repayment. Therefore, the appellant asserted its rights against the debtor within the statutory period, and the principal debt has not exceeded the statute of limitations. According to Article 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Notice on Issues Concerning the Guarantee Period for Guaranty Acts Occurring Before the Effective Date of the Security Law, the appellant asserted its rights within six months after the issuance of that notice. Times Company should bear liability. 3. The first instance judgment found that on January 23, 1995, Animal Products Company used USD 1,169,422.31 and USD 340,692.60 to repay USD 1,500,000 under the loan contract numbered 94010 in two installments. This fact was based on two repayment vouchers that the court itself collected after the conclusion of the trial at first instance, which were not subject to cross-examination, violating legal procedures.

Huaxi Group did not submit a written reply to the court but argued at trial: Animal Products Company and Huaxi Group are two independent legal persons, and there is no fact that Animal Products Company invested all its assets into Huaxi Group. Provincial BOC made the loan to Animal Products Company after Huaxi Group was established; Animal Products Company is the party to the loan contract. As for Huaxi Group's application for extension of the USD 2,000,000 loan in its own name to Provincial BOC, this was because during the planned economy period, both Animal Products Company and Huaxi Group were enterprises under government supervision. It occurred in a specific historical period, and the application was not agreed to by Provincial BOC, nor did it imply that Huaxi Group replaced Animal Products Company as the borrower. This application has no legal significance.

Animal Products Company did not submit a written reply but argued at trial: The appellant's statements are inconsistent with the facts. Animal Products Company's assets and operations were not merged into Huaxi Group; it continues to exist. Animal Products Company's debts should be repaid by Animal Products Company itself, and have no relation to Huaxi Group.

Times Company did not submit a written reply but argued at trial: There was no agreement between Provincial BOC and the debtor for an extension of repayment. The principal debt has exceeded the statute of limitations, and the guarantor should be exempted from guarantee liability in accordance with the law.

In addition to the facts found by the court of first instance, this Court found the following facts on appeal: Animal Products Company is the sole core enterprise of Huaxi Group. For a certain period after its establishment, the legal representatives of Huaxi Group and Animal Products Company were the same person, and they operated at the same location. The detailed list of registered capital of Huaxi Group's enterprise registration records that the fixed assets of Huaxi Group included property of Animal Products Company and its subordinate branches. On July 7, 1995, Huaxi Group sent an "Application for Extension of USD Loan" to Provincial BOC, which stated: "Our company borrowed USD 2,000,000 from your department on January 14, 1995 (Hui Liu Zi No. 95001) for importing mink and fox skins for processing and exporting garments... the loan matured and we have no funds to repay it, so we specially apply to your department for an extension of this loan..." The above facts are supported by evidence including the registration documents for the establishment of Huaxi Group, the detailed list of registered capital, and the "Application for Extension of USD Loan."

This Court holds: The loan contracts numbered 95001 and 97000538 signed between Animal Products Company and Provincial BOC, the irrevocable letter of guarantee issued by Times Company, and the creditor's rights transfer agreement between Provincial BOC and Orient Company are not disputed by any party. All of these agreements are the true expressions of the parties' intentions, do not violate prohibitive provisions of laws and regulations, and are legal and valid. The first instance judgment's determination of the validity of the above agreements and that Animal Products Company should bear the liability for repayment of the loans under the two loan contracts numbered 95001 and 97000538 is correct, and this Court affirms it.

The guarantee letter of Times Company promised that it would be "effective from the date of signing and automatically expire when all principal, interest and expenses owed by the borrower are fully repaid." This constitutes an unclear agreement on the guarantee period. According to Article 1 of this Court's Notice (2002) No. 144 on Issues Concerning the Guarantee Period for Guaranty Acts Occurring Before the Effective Date of the Security Law, the creditor may assert its rights against the guarantor within six months after the issuance of that notice. Orient Company filed a lawsuit with the court of first instance on August 8, 2002, which complies with the spirit of that notice. The loan contract numbered 95001 matured on July 14, 1995. The debtor, Animal Products Company, repaid five installments of loan interest to Provincial BOC from June 15, 1995 to July 31, 1996. Therefore, the statute of limitations for the principal debt should start from August 1, 1996 and expire on July 31, 1998. Upon review, there is no evidence to prove an agreed extension of repayment between Provincial BOC and Animal Products Company. Provincial BOC sent loan collection notices to Animal Products Company on August 31, 1999 and September 13, 1999. Accordingly, Provincial BOC's creditor's rights against Animal Products Company had exceeded the statute of limitations, and the debtor acquired the defense of expiration of the limitation period in accordance with law. However, Provincial BOC twice sent collection notices to Animal Products Company on August 31, 1999 and September 13, 1999, and Animal Products Company affixed its seal to each notice. According to the provisions of this Court's Reply (Fa Shi (1999) No. 7) on the Legal Effect of a Borrower's Signing or Sealing on a Payment Reminder After the Statute of Limitations Has Expired, Animal Products Company's affixing its seal on the collection notices should be deemed a reaffirmation of the original debt. Therefore, the creditor's rights are still protected by law. According to this judicial interpretation, the borrower Animal Products Company's act of sealing the collection notices constituted a waiver of the defense of expiration of the statute of limitations for the original debt. The first instance court's judgment that Animal Products Company should bear the liability to repay the original debt complies with the judicial interpretation and should be affirmed.

Guarantor Shidai Company explicitly undertook in the Irrevocable Letter of Guarantee: "This Letter of Guarantee shall remain valid if the Bank of China agrees to extend the repayment period." However, as there is no evidence to prove that the Liaoning Branch of Bank of China and the Animal Products Company agreed to extend the repayment of the debt, the principal claim has exceeded the statute of limitations. Pursuant to Article 20, paragraph 1 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Guarantee Law), the guarantor acquired the right to plead the expiration of the statute of limitations for the principal claim enjoyed by the principal debtor. Although the Animal Products Company subsequently affixed its seal on the collection notice, thereby waiving the defense based on the expiration of the statute of limitations for the original claim, in accordance with Article 20, paragraph 1 of the Guarantee Law, the guarantor may still exercise the defense waived by the debtor. The act of the Animal Products Company in waiving the defense based on the expiration of the statute of limitations has no legal effect on Shidai Company. In addition, Article 1 of the Notice of this Court (2002) No. 144 stipulates that a creditor's rights against a guarantor shall be conditioned on the principal debt not exceeding the statute of limitations period. Therefore, the appellant Dongfang Company's ground for appeal that the guarantor Shidai Company should bear the guarantee liability cannot be established. The judgment of the first instance is correct, and this Court affirms it.

Huaxi Group was established upon the application of the Animal Products Company, which was the sole core enterprise of Huaxi Group. The registered capital of Huaxi Group included the fixed assets of the Animal Products Company and its branches. The two companies also once shared the same office location and legal representative. Therefore, it can be determined that a certain affiliated relationship existed between the two companies. After the loan under Loan Contract No. 95001 matured, Huaxi Group issued to the Liaoning Branch of Bank of China the Application for Extension of US Dollar Loan. According to the contents of that application, Huaxi Group used the loan under Loan Contract No. 95001 to import mink and fox skins for processing and export of garments. Huaxi Group was the actual user of the loan, and in that application, Huaxi Group also acknowledged itself as the borrower. This Court is of the opinion that, based on the basic fact that an affiliated relationship existed between Huaxi Group and the Animal Products Company, and the Application for Extension of US Dollar Loan issued by Huaxi Group to the Liaoning Branch of Bank of China, in the borrowing relationship formed by Loan Contract No. 95001, there was a factual confusion of borrower identity between Huaxi Group and the Animal Products Company, and thus they constituted a joint debtor relationship. Huaxi Group shall bear the legal liability to repay the loan together with the Animal Products Company. The judgment of the first instance that Huaxi Group did not bear liability for the principal and interest of the loan under Loan Contract No. 95001 shall be corrected.

In the borrowing relationship formed by Loan Contract No. 97000538 between the Liaoning Branch of Bank of China and the Animal Products Company, there is currently insufficient evidence to prove that Huaxi Group and the Animal Products Company constituted a joint debtor relationship. The appellant Dongfang Company's appeal request that Huaxi Group bear liability for repaying the loan under that loan contract lacks sufficient factual and legal basis, and this Court does not support it.

The judgment of the first instance found that the Animal Products Company used part of the loan of USD 2,000,000 to repay its old loans with the Liaoning Branch of Bank of China. This fact is relevant to whether the guarantor Shidai Company has the right to the defense of exemption due to "borrowing new loans to repay old ones." Dongfang Company appealed requesting this Court to review the validity of the evidence collected by the court of first instance. This Court is of the opinion that the court of first instance's collection of evidence did not violate the provisions of China's Civil Procedure Law. However, since Shidai Company's guarantee liability has been discharged because the guaranteed principal claim has exceeded the statute of limitations period, whether this fact is confirmed or not does not affect the outcome of this case. This Court will not review or confirm this fact and its corresponding legal consequences. In addition, as to the amount of loan interest involved in the judgment of the first instance, since none of the parties raised any objection, this Court will not adjudicate it.

In conclusion, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, items (1) and (2) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this Court hereby renders judgment as follows:

1. Affirm items one, two, and three of the main text of the Civil Judgment (2002) Liao Min San Chu Zi No. 70 of the Liaoning High People's Court.

2. Amend item four of the main text of the above judgment to: Liaoning Huaxi Group Company shall bear joint and several liability for the debt confirmed in item one of the main text of the above judgment against Liaoning Province Animal Products Import and Export Company.

The above judgment shall be performed within 10 days from the day following the date of receipt of this judgment. For late performance, the matter shall be handled in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

The first-instance case acceptance fee is RMB 158,640, and the preservation fee is RMB 152,760, to be borne jointly by Liaoning Huaxi Group Company and Liaoning Province Animal Products Import and Export Company. The second-instance case acceptance fee is RMB 158,640, to be borne by China Orient Asset Management Corporation Dalian Office in the amount of RMB 79,320, and jointly by Liaoning Huaxi Group Company and Liaoning Province Animal Products Import and Export Company in the amount of RMB 79,320.

This judgment is final.

Presiding Judge: Jiang Bixin

Judge: Song Xiaoming

Judge: Cao Shibing

August 28, 2003

Clerk: Xia Dongxia

[Introduction to the Presiding Judge]

Justice Jiang Bixin: Born in 1956, Master of Laws. Formerly served as Deputy Chief Judge of the Administrative Division of the Supreme People's Court, Chief Judge of the Administrative Division, and Member of the Judicial Committee. Appointed Vice President of the Supreme People's Court in 2002, and concurrently served as Chairman of the Compensation Committee of the Supreme People's Court from 2003.
